persona: Researcher tuning 5 numeric parameters of a NOISY black-box objective (synthetic, known ground truth: true loss default=1.4862, optimum=0, 'slightly better' config gap=0.30, Gaussian noise sd=0.9 on the reported mean = 3x the gap), using only param_lhs / zero-LLM, who cares whether the reported winner is REALLY better than the default.
journey: Read README.md, docs/new-experiment.md, AGENTS.md, examples/pyvrp (README, both configs, the # PARAMS evolve block) and all --help output. Ran `evolvekit init noisy/` in my scratch dir, wrote skeleton.py (ALPHA, BETA, LR, K int, USE_TRICK 0/1 under a `# PARAMS:` line + get_params()) and evaluate.py (smooth quadratic in normalised/log coords, noise seeded by (seed, inputs, params), list KPI loss_per_instance, honours --seed). Preflight was clean. First run with `operators: {param_lhs: 1.0}` died at gen 3 with a raw traceback: the scheduled big step needed the fake provider's fake_responses.yaml, which init references but never writes. `big_step_every: 0` is a config error; 9999 got me a full zero-LLM run (~4 min after starting the docs). Later a 50-generation run died again at gen 26: a plateau-triggered big step fires after patience/2 flat generations regardless of operator weights. Resuming that run replayed the same LHS samples (89/100, then 20/20 structural duplicates). Ran seeds:1 and seeds:5 (12 gens x 4 children) plus a 200-child run, then computed true losses and re-evaluated winner and default on 30 fresh seeds. Result: every reported improvement was selection noise (+0.286, +0.937, +0.352 reported vs -0.135, -0.135, +0.008 true). No view shows n/sd/CI; kpi_cv lives only in runs.jsonl. Probed PARAMS syntax: ints and 0/1 work; log-scale guesses, reversed ranges, bool constants are silently frozen; JSON bools/bad JSON silently disable the operator. Measured that param_lhs samples the whole box uniformly, ignoring the parent. Found two documented mechanisms that can be repurposed as noise guards (private hold-out with independent noise; 1-seed proxy -> 10-seed full cascade) - both honestly reported improvement 0 - and an undocumented validation route via `preflight --candidate` with a seeds:30 config and my own --seed-offset flag. Checked status mid-run, the lock, and export paths. All work stayed in the scratch dir; my one background run (pid recorded from .lock: 2796) exited before I finished. Note: `git status` at the end showed ` M docs/mission/DECISION_LOG.md` in the repo - not touched by me (another job on the machine). Never read evolvekit/*.py or tests/.

entries.title: Reported 'best' and 'improvement' are pure winner's curse on a noisy objective; no documented way to confirm a winner on fresh seeds or re-evaluate the incumbent
entries.step: Run param_lhs-only search with seeds:1 and seeds:5, then check the reported winner against ground truth and 30 fresh seeds
entries.command:
python -m evolvekit run --config cfg_bs9999.yaml --run-dir runs/bs9999 --generations 12   (seeds: 1)
python -m evolvekit run --config cfg_seeds5.yaml --run-dir runs/seeds5 --generations 12   (seeds: 5)
python -m evolvekit run --config cfg_long2.yaml --run-dir runs/long200b --generations 50   (seeds: 1, 200 children)
python analyze.py runs/<dir> 30   (my script: true loss + 30 fresh seeds 1000..1029)
python -m evolvekit preflight --config cfg_seeds5.yaml --candidate runs/seeds5/work/candidates/g002-c0006.py
entries.observed:
seeds:1 (48 children): summary 'seed score : -0.228169 / best score : 0.057832 / improvement : 0.286001'. TRUE loss: default 1.4862, reported best g002-c0006 1.6214 -> true improvement -0.135 (winner is WORSE). Optimism of best = +1.68 (~1.9 noise sd). 30 fresh seeds: default 1.335+-0.169, best 1.605+-0.178, default-best = -0.270+-0.252.
seeds:5: 'seed score : -1.55498 / best score : -0.617717 / improvement : 0.937' (not printed with any caveat). Same candidate, TRUE improvement -0.135; optimism +1.00 = 2.5 SE at n=5. 0 of 48 children were truly better than the default.
200 children, seeds:1: 'best score : 0.124204 improvement : 0.352373' (a loss of -0.124 on a function whose true minimum is 0). TRUE improvement +0.008. The truly best evaluated candidate g023-c0093 (true 0.595, a real 0.89 gain) was reported rank 8.
The seed's own 1-seed score (0.228 vs true 1.486) is a lucky draw that is never re-evaluated, so it acts as a false bar for the whole run.
`preflight --candidate <winner>` with the run's config prints 'loss=0.617717 (cv 67.88%)' - byte-identical to the run, because every evaluation uses seeds 0..N-1. There is no --seeds/--seed-offset/validate command; README/docs contain no mention of re-evaluation, incumbents, confirmation or held-out seeds (grep).
entries.expected: A documented confirm step: e.g. `evolvekit validate --run-dir R --top 3 --seeds 30 --fresh` that re-runs the top-k AND the seed on seeds disjoint from those used in selection and prints mean +- SE and a paired difference vs the seed; or an option to re-evaluate the incumbent/elite periodically; at minimum a run-summary caveat when a seeds-stage's SE is larger than the claimed improvement.
entries.why_it_matters: The one number this persona came for - 'is the winner really better than the default?' - is answered wrongly (+0.94 reported, -0.14 true) and silently. Anyone shipping the reported winner would ship a config that is worse than the default.
entries.suggested_fix: Add a `validate` (or `leaderboard --revalidate`) command that evaluates top-k + seed on fresh seeds (seed offset beyond any used in the run) and reports mean, sd, n, SE and paired delta vs seed. Let `{seed}` take an offset/base from config (`seed_base:`) so held-out seeds are possible without editing the evaluator. Print 'improvement X is within ~k SE of noise' in the run summary when kpi spread is available. Document the hold-out-with-independent-noise and proxy(1 seed)->full(N seeds) cascade patterns as the recommended setup for noisy objectives (both reported 'improvement : 0' correctly in my tests).

entries.title: No uncertainty shown next to 'best' anywhere; kpi_cv exists only as raw JSON, is a CV (meaningless near zero), and n is not recorded
entries.step: Look for CI / std / n beside the best score in run summary, status, leaderboard and HTML dashboard after a seeds:5 run
entries.command:
python -m evolvekit status --run-dir runs/seeds5
python -m evolvekit leaderboard --run-dir runs/seeds5 --limit 5 --html runs/seeds5/board.html
grep -o -i -E "kpi_cv|\bcv\b|std|seeds|±|confidence|n=" runs/seeds5/board.html | sort | uniq -c
python -m evolvekit preflight --config cfg_seeds5.yaml --candidate optimum_candidate.py
entries.observed: status: 'best         : g002-c0006 rank=-0.617717 score=-0.617717 cell=[3]' - nothing else. Leaderboard columns: '# | id | gen | rank | score | cell | operator | model | lineage | gap | USD'. HTML: 49 hits for kpi_cv, all inside `<script id="rows" type="application/json">`; table headers have no cv/sd/n column. Only runs.jsonl has 'kpi_cv': {'loss': 0.6788...}; the row has no seeds/n field, so SE cannot be derived from the row alone. I had to compute from work/stage_out/*.seed*.json that kpi_cv = sample stdev / mean (0.678834 matched stdev/mean, not pstdev/mean) -> best = 0.618 +- 0.188 SE. For the true optimum (true loss 0) preflight prints 'loss=0.175313 (cv 275.72%)' and 'the noisiest KPI varied by 275.72%' - CV explodes for a KPI near zero and changes sign for negative means (a reported mean of -0.0578 occurred). The list KPI loss_per_instance I emitted is dropped from runs.jsonl kpis and used for no spread estimate.
entries.expected: Leaderboard/status/summary show 'mean +- SE (n=5)' for best and seed, and the improvement with its SE. Row records n, sd (not only cv) per KPI.
entries.why_it_matters: README says kpi_cv 'is there so a human can see when the mean was a coin toss', but no human-facing view shows it; a researcher reading the board sees six-significant-digit scores and no hint that the top two rows are statistically indistinguishable.
entries.suggested_fix: Store kpi_sd, kpi_n (and per-seed values) on the candidate row; add '+-SE' and 'n' columns to markdown/HTML leaderboards and to the status 'best' line; print 'improvement : 0.937 +- 0.55 (n=5 vs n=5)' in the summary. Keep cv only as a secondary figure and suppress it when |mean| is small relative to sd.

entries.title: A zero-LLM (param_lhs-only) run is not actually supported: big steps cannot be disabled and a plateau big step fires regardless of operator weights
entries.step: Configure a run that never calls a model: operators {param_lhs: 1.0}, then try to switch off big_step
entries.command:
python -m evolvekit run --config evolvekit.yaml --run-dir runs/s1-first            (big_step_every: 3)
python -m evolvekit run --config cfg_bs0.yaml --run-dir runs/bs0 --generations 4      (big_step_every: 0)
python -m evolvekit run --config cfg_pat8.yaml --run-dir runs/pat8 --generations 20    (big_step_every: 9999, patience: 8)
python -m evolvekit run --config cfg_long.yaml --run-dir runs/long200 --generations 50 (big_step_every: 9999, patience: 50)
entries.observed:
big_step_every: 3 -> crash while breeding gen 3: 'evolvekit.providers.base.ProviderError: fake provider: responses_path not found: ...\noisy\fake_responses.yaml' (traceback through driver._breed(generation, plateau=decision.plateau)).
big_step_every: 0 -> 'config error: search.big_step_every: must be >= 1, got 0'.
big_step_every: 9999, patience: 8 -> gens 1-4 run, then same ProviderError traceback after gen 4.
big_step_every: 9999, patience: 50 -> gens 1-25 run (100 evaluations), then same traceback at gen 26. I.e. a plateau big step calls the strong model after patience/2 flat generations (observed at 8->4 and 50->25) even though search.operators lists only param_lhs. Only patience >= 2x generations kept the run LLM-free.
entries.expected: The docs to say whether a zero-LLM run is possible and how: e.g. `big_step_every: 0`/`big_step: off`, or 'if only param_lhs has weight, no model is ever called'. With a paid provider this would be silent spend the user explicitly tried to avoid.
entries.why_it_matters: A numeric-tuning user with no API key cannot trust a long run to finish; on a noisy objective plateaus are the normal state (the seed's lucky score is rarely beaten), so the hidden LLM call is nearly guaranteed. With the init scaffold's `patience: 4` it would fire after ~2 flat generations.
entries.suggested_fix: Allow `search.big_step_every: 0` (and a `search.plateau_big_step: false`) and skip big steps automatically when no LLM operator has weight; document 'Zero-LLM runs' in README next to the param_lhs section; make `models` optional in that mode. preflight should warn 'this config can call models.strong on plateau' when only param_lhs is weighted.

entries.title: `init` scaffold points both fake models at fake_responses.yaml but does not write it; preflight says 'clean'; the run later dies with an uncaught traceback
entries.step: Follow init's 'Next:' instructions and run preflight then run
entries.command:
python -m evolvekit init noisy/
python -m evolvekit preflight --config evolvekit.yaml
python -m evolvekit run --config evolvekit.yaml --run-dir runs/s1-first
entries.observed:
init: 'wrote ...evolvekit.yaml / wrote ....env.example / Next: point problem.skeleton at your skeleton file, then python -m evolvekit run --config evolvekit.yaml' (no fake_responses.yaml written or mentioned; scaffold has `options: responses_path: fake_responses.yaml` twice).
preflight: 'verdict : clean (0 failure(s), 0 warning(s))'.
run: 30-line Python traceback ending 'evolvekit.providers.base.ProviderError: fake provider: responses_path not found: ...\noisy\fake_responses.yaml', exit 1, printed BEFORE the buffered 'gen 0 seed score=...' lines. In a later run the same crash arrived at generation 26 after 100 evaluations. The fake_responses format (keyed `when:`/`response:` entries plus a queue of bare strings) is only discoverable from examples/*/fake_responses.yaml; README has one table row about it.
entries.expected: init writes a minimal fake_responses.yaml (or the fake provider tolerates a missing file until first use with a one-line error); load_config/preflight fails fast on a missing responses_path; provider errors are reported as 'error: ...' like the lock and config errors are, not as a traceback.
entries.why_it_matters: The documented offline path fails on the first attempt, and because the file is only opened on the first LLM call the failure can land deep into an expensive run rather than at start-up.
entries.suggested_fix: Validate `options.responses_path` exists in load_config (key-path error like other config errors); have `init` emit a stub fake_responses.yaml with one commented example; catch ProviderError in cmd_run and print a one-line message plus 'the run dir is resumable'.

entries.title: `# PARAMS:` problems fail silently: unsupported specs freeze a parameter at its default or disable the operator, with no warning in preflight or run
entries.step: Find out whether log-scale, bool and int ranges work by trying plausible PARAMS spellings (docs only show `{"NAME": [lo, hi]}`)
entries.command: for v in log3 logdict bool boolconst reversed missing badjson; do python -m evolvekit run --config cfg_$v.yaml --run-dir runs/var-$v --generations 1; done   (each config = same problem, one-line change to the PARAMS line or a constant)
entries.observed:
"LR": [1e-5, 1e-1, "log"]  -> exit 0, no message; every child has 'LR = 0.01' (LR silently not swept; other params swept).
"LR": {"range": [1e-5, 1e-1], "scale": "log"} -> same: LR = 0.01 in all children, no message.
"ALPHA": [10.0, 0.0] (reversed) -> exit 0; 'ALPHA = 5.0' in all children, no message.
constant `USE_TRICK = False` with range [0, 1] -> 'USE_TRICK = False' in all children, no message.
undeclared name "GAMMA": [0.0, 1.0] (typo case) -> silently ignored.
"USE_TRICK": [false, true] -> whole PARAMS line apparently rejected: gen 1 falls through to an LLM operator and dies with 'ProviderError: fake provider: responses_path not found' - nothing mentions PARAMS.
malformed JSON (double comma) -> same misleading ProviderError traceback.
Working cases (went well): int constant + [1, 64] yields ints incl. endpoints (K=1 x5, K=64 x1 in 200); 0/1 int flag balanced 97/103. LR [1e-5, 0.1] is sampled linearly: 1 of 200 samples < 1e-3, 18 < 1e-2, 0 < 1e-4.
entries.expected: preflight (which costs nothing) lists 'param_lhs will sweep: ALPHA[0,10] float, K[1,64] int, ...' and warns per parameter that was declared but skipped and why; an unparseable PARAMS line is a config/preflight failure. A documented log-scale and bool/categorical syntax.
entries.why_it_matters: A learning-rate-like parameter spanning 4 decades is the most common thing a tuner declares; guessing a log syntax silently removes it from the search and the user believes it was tuned. With a paid provider an invalid PARAMS line silently converts a free run into LLM spend.
entries.suggested_fix: Validate the PARAMS line at load/preflight with key-path errors (`PARAMS.LR: expected [lo, hi] with lo < hi, got [...]`); warn on declared-but-missing constants and on constants whose literal type is unsupported; print the swept set in preflight and in traces; add `[lo, hi, "log"]`, `[false, true]` and `{"choices": [...]}` forms and document int rounding semantics.

entries.title: param_lhs does not exploit: it samples the whole declared box uniformly and ignores the parent, so on this problem 2 of 200 children truly beat the default
entries.step: Measure how param_lhs children relate to their parent and to the declared ranges
entries.command: python -m evolvekit run --config cfg_bs9999.yaml --run-dir runs/bs9999 --generations 12 ; python -m evolvekit run --config cfg_long2.yaml --run-dir runs/long200b --generations 50 ; then my script grouping child constants by parent_id from runs.jsonl
entries.observed: Parent g002-c0006 (ALPHA=4.229, BETA=-1.254, LR=0.000556, K=27), 26 children: ALPHA min 0.318 / mean 4.65 / max 9.818; BETA -4.815..4.371; LR 0.00268..0.0982 (mean 0.044, 80x the parent's); K 2..62. Children of the seed look the same. 200-child run: ALPHA per-unit-bin counts [22,27,13,19,17,19,20,17,25,21] (a real 200-point LHS would give 20 each, so stratification buys nothing across a run); 2/200 children truly better than the default (true loss < 1.4862), 0/48 in the 12-generation runs. The leaderboard still prints a lineage ('g002-c0006 < g000-c0001') and the archive does parent sampling, implying inheritance that does not exist for this operator.
entries.expected: Either local perturbation around the selected parent (shrinking trust region / Gaussian step scaled to range) mixed with global draws, or documentation saying plainly 'param_lhs is global uniform random sampling; the parent only supplies the code around the constants'.
entries.why_it_matters: README sells it as the free operator for 15-minute evaluations ('a free child is worth having'). For numeric tuning it is random search in a 5-D box: evaluation budget is spent far from the incumbent, so true improvements are rare and the noisy-best is almost always a lucky bad point.
entries.suggested_fix: Add a `param_local` mode (perturb parent's values by N(0, sigma*range), sigma annealed, respecting int/log) and/or a simple model-based proposer; make the LHS a real batch design per generation (one stratum per child) and state the distribution in the README.

entries.title: Resuming a param_lhs run replays the same sample sequence: 89/100 and then 20/20 children rejected as structural duplicates
entries.step: Re-run the same --run-dir after the plateau-big-step crash, as the docs advise ('resume cleanly in the same --run-dir')
entries.command:
python -m evolvekit run --config cfg_long.yaml --run-dir runs/long200 --generations 50   (2nd invocation)
python -m evolvekit run --config cfg_long.yaml --run-dir runs/long200 --generations 5    (3rd invocation)
entries.observed:
2nd invocation: 'resumed 101 candidate(s) from runs.jsonl' then 'g026-c0102 duplicate after 1 attempt(s): duplicate: structurally identical to g001-c0003', 'g027-c0106 ... identical to g002-c0008', 'g030-c0118..0121 identical to g005-c0018..0021', ... -> 89 of 100 new children rejected, never evaluated; crashed again at the next plateau big step.
3rd invocation: 'resumed 201 candidate(s)'; all 20/20 children duplicates (g051-c0202 identical to g001-c0003, g055-c0218..0221 identical to g005-c0018..0021); summary 'rejected : 109 (0 no-op, 109 duplicate, 0 behavioural)'. (In another run where the best had changed before the resume only 1 of 24 was a duplicate, so it depends on parent selection repeating.) Also: `--generations 6` on a resumed dir ran gens 4..9, i.e. it means '6 more', which no help text says.
entries.expected: Resume continues the sampling stream (persist RNG state / derive the draw from the global candidate counter) so resumed generations produce new points.
entries.why_it_matters: After a crash the generation budget is burned on replays; each further resume restarts the same sequence, so a param_lhs-only run whose incumbent does not change can never get past what the longest single invocation reached.
entries.suggested_fix: Seed each param_lhs draw from (search.seed, candidate index) or persist the RNG state in archive.json/runs.jsonl; on duplicate, redraw instead of spending the child; document --generations semantics on resume in `run --help`.

entries.title: No way to export the winning parameter VALUES; they must be scraped from code or from an undocumented trace field
entries.step: Get the best candidate's parameters as JSON/YAML/CLI flags
entries.command: python -m evolvekit status --run-dir runs/seeds5 ; python -m evolvekit leaderboard --run-dir runs/seeds5 --limit 5 ; python -m evolvekit leaderboard --help
entries.observed: status/leaderboard give only the id ('best : g002-c0006 rank=-0.617717 ...'); no subcommand or flag exports a candidate (subcommands: init, preflight, run, status, leaderboard). I found three manual routes: (a) exec the 'block' string from runs.jsonl and call get_params(); (b) import <run_dir>/work/candidates/g002-c0006.py - a path README's run-directory description never mentions; (c) traces/g002-c0006.json has 'meta': {'operator': 'param_lhs', 'params': {'ALPHA': 4.22902, 'BETA': -1.254122, 'LR': 0.000556, 'K': 27, 'USE_TRICK': 1}} - usable JSON, but README describes traces only as 'the exact messages sent and the response received', and the seed / any LLM-written child has no such field.
entries.expected: `python -m evolvekit best --run-dir R [--format json|yaml|flags|py]` printing the PARAMS values of the best (or any id), plus the full candidate source path.
entries.why_it_matters: For parameter tuning the deliverable is a dict of numbers to paste into another system, not a Python block; every user will write the same regex/exec hack.
entries.suggested_fix: Add an export/best subcommand that parses the PARAMS constants out of any candidate block (the framework already knows how, since param_lhs rewrites them) and emits JSON/YAML/`--name value` flags; record 'params' on every runs.jsonl row whose block has a PARAMS line; document work/candidates/.

entries.title: Leaderboard ranks 1-seed proxy-only scores and N-seed full-stage scores in one column with no stage or n shown
entries.step: Use the documented cascade as a racing scheme for noise: proxy seeds:1 with promote top 1/generation, full seeds:10
entries.command: python -m evolvekit run --config cfg_cascade.yaml --run-dir runs/cascade --generations 12 --quiet ; python -m evolvekit leaderboard --run-dir runs/cascade --limit 16
entries.observed: Rows 1-10 are full-stage (10-seed means), row 11 'g010-c0038 | 10 | -2.87294 | -2.87294' is a proxy-only single-seed score, row 12-16 likewise; the table has no column saying which stage produced 'score' or how many seeds back it. Only runs.jsonl 'stages_reached'/'stage_scores' tells them apart (e.g. g008-c0030 proxy=-1.185 but full=-2.864: a lucky proxy draw 1.7 better than its 10-seed mean).
entries.expected: A 'stage' (deepest stage reached) and 'n' column, or separate sections per stage, so a 1-sample score is never read as comparable to a 10-sample mean.
entries.why_it_matters: On a noisy objective the deepest-stage/n information is exactly what decides whether a row can be trusted; a lucky unpromoted proxy score can sit above validated candidates.
entries.suggested_fix: Add 'stage' and 'seeds' columns to both leaderboards and to the status best line; optionally rank only candidates that reached the final stage by default.

entries.title: `status` cannot tell a finished run from a crashed or a live one, and does not record the stop reason
entries.step: Check the state of runs after the terminal output is gone (one finished, one crashed with a traceback, one still running)
entries.command: python -m evolvekit status --run-dir runs/live   (finished) ; python -m evolvekit status --run-dir runs/pat8   (crashed) ; same command against runs/live while it was running
entries.observed: All three print the same fields (candidates / novelty / behavioural / near-dupes / generations / archive / best / llm calls / tokens / spend + economics table). The crashed and the in-progress run differ only by 'archive : no archive.json snapshot yet'. No 'state: running (pid 2796) | finished: generations exhausted | crashed: ProviderError ...' line, no last-activity time, no target generation count. The stop reason exists only in the run's stdout.
entries.expected: A state line derived from .lock (pid alive?) plus a persisted stop reason / last error and 'generation 6 of 10'.
entries.why_it_matters: With hour-long evaluators and overnight runs the first question next morning is 'did it finish, and why did it stop?'; today that needs the scrollback.
entries.suggested_fix: Write a small run_state.json (started, last_generation, target, stop_reason, last_error) at each generation and on exit/exception; have status print it together with lock liveness.

entries.title: Small doc/help inaccuracies around run directories and run options
entries.step: Locate a saved candidate for `preflight --candidate` and understand `run` options
entries.command: python -m evolvekit preflight --help ; python -m evolvekit run --help ; ls runs/seeds5
entries.observed: preflight --help: '--candidate PATH dry-run this candidate's full source (as saved under a run's candidates/ directory)' - the real location is <run_dir>/work/candidates/<id>.py. README's run-directory paragraph lists runs.jsonl, usage.jsonl, archive.json, scratchpad.md, .lock, traces/ but not work/ (candidates/, stage_out/ with per-seed JSON incl. list KPIs). `run --help` lists --config/--run-dir/--generations/--quiet with no description at all (so '--generations = N more on resume' and '--quiet still prints the summary' are discoveries).
entries.expected: Help text and README that match the on-disk layout and describe each option.
entries.why_it_matters: Minutes lost hunting for the candidate file that the only validation-capable command needs.
entries.suggested_fix: Fix the path in the --candidate help, add work/candidates and work/stage_out to the README run-dir description, add help strings to the run options.

entries.title: Defaults that misread a pure-parameter problem: `complexity` descriptor splits cells on the sign of a constant; minimise objectives are shown as unlabeled negated 'score'
entries.step: Read the archive and summary lines of a param_lhs-only run using the scaffold's default descriptor
entries.observed: 'archive : 2/4 cells occupied (complexity[4])' - the two cells are complexity 44 vs 46: a negative literal (BETA = -1.03) adds two AST nodes, so the MAP-Elites grid partitions candidates by the sign of BETA. Summary prints 'best score : 0.124204' for a loss of -0.124 (direction: minimize -> score = -loss) with no KPI name or direction on the summary, status or leaderboard.
entries.expected: Docs to suggest a descriptor for parameter-tuning problems (e.g. a normalised parameter as a KPI) or to say the archive is irrelevant for param_lhs; summaries to label 'loss (minimize)' and show the KPI in its own units.
entries.why_it_matters: Minor confusion when cross-checking evolvekit's numbers against one's own re-evaluations (sign flips), and a meaningless 'cells' statistic.
entries.suggested_fix: Show 'objective loss = 0.6177 (minimize; score -0.6177)' in summary/status; mention in the param_lhs docs that complexity is not a useful axis for constant-only blocks.

unanswered_questions: Is the reported best statistically better than the seed/default? (no SE, CI, n or test anywhere in summary, status, leaderboard or HTML)
How many seeds and which stage stand behind each score on the leaderboard?
Was the seed's own score a lucky or unlucky draw - what would the incumbent score if re-evaluated? (seed reported 0.228 on 1 seed vs true 1.486)

How do I evaluate the winner and the default on seeds that were NOT used during selection, using evolvekit itself? (only found an undocumented workaround: a second config with seeds: 30 + my own --seed-offset flag + preflight --candidate)
How do I tell the search the objective is noisy beyond `seeds: N` - e.g. how should stop.epsilon relate to the noise sd, and does anything re-test elites?
Is kpi_cv a sample or population sd over the mean, and what n produced it? (had to recompute from work/stage_out files: sample stdev/mean; n is not in the row)
Which PARAMS entries did param_lhs actually sweep in this run, and which did it silently skip?
Does param_lhs sample around the parent or over the whole range, and with what distribution (linear/log, int rounding)? (had to measure: global, uniform, linear)
Is a fully zero-LLM run supported, and exactly when does a plateau-triggered big step fire? (observed after patience/2 flat generations; not documented)
Did my run finish, crash, or is it still running, and what was the stop reason - after the terminal output is gone?
What are the best candidate's parameter values, as data rather than code?
Does `--generations N` on a resumed run dir mean 'up to N' or 'N more'? (observed: N more)
Why did resumed generations replay earlier samples, and how do I resume a param_lhs run without that?
went_well: Docs + `init` + examples/pyvrp got my own problem through preflight and a first complete zero-LLM run in about 4 minutes; the evaluator contract ({candidate}/{out}/{inputs}/{seed}, JSON with kpis + text_feedback, 'accept --seed even if you ignore it') is clear and correct.

`seeds: N` behaves exactly as documented: every candidate is evaluated on the same seeds 0..N-1 (verified 49/49 candidates had seed0..seed4 outputs), per-seed JSON is kept in work/stage_out/<id>.<stage>.seed<k>.json, the KPI is the mean and kpi_cv matched sample stdev/mean to 6 digits.
preflight on a seeds:N stage surfaces noise early: 'loss=1.55498 (cv 73.69%)' and 'the noisiest KPI varied by 73.69% across them'.
The README is honest about the limitation ('the search ranks by the mean, and kpi_cv is there so a human can see when the mean was a coin toss').
Integer and 0/1 parameters work with the documented [lo, hi] form: an int constant with [1, 64] yields ints including both endpoints (K=1 x5, K=64 x1 of 200); a 0/1 int flag came out 97/103.
Runs are reproducible: the same search.seed gave identical LHS samples across configs, which made seeds:1 vs seeds:5 directly comparable.

Two documented mechanisms can be repurposed as noise guards and both gave the honest answer 'improvement : 0': a private_inputs hold-out whose noise is independent (ranking = min(public, private) at holdout_penalty 1.0), and a 1-seed proxy -> promote -> 10-seed full cascade (top-5 order then agreed with the true ordering).

`preflight --config validate.yaml --candidate <winner.py>` with seeds: 30 reproduced my independent 30-fresh-seed re-evaluation exactly (winner 1.60523, default 1.33531 vs my 1.6052 / 1.3353) - a workable, if undocumented, validation path.
Structural duplicates are rejected before evaluation, so the replayed samples after resume cost no evaluator time.
Run lock and live status work: a second run against a live dir was refused with a clear message naming the pid and the fix; `status` works mid-run; the lock was gone after the run finished.
param_lhs really is free: every run reported 'spend : $0.0000 over 0 call(s), 0 token(s)', and traces/<id>.json records the drawn params as JSON for param_lhs children.
Config validation messages are good where they exist: 'config error: search.big_step_every: must be >= 1, got 0' (exit 2).
